title: Superconducting diode effect via Floquet topological Fulde-Ferrell phase in driven Rashba nanowire
authors: Sayak Bhowmik, Arijit Saha, Tanay Nag
abstract: Much has been studied on Floquet engineering in Rashba nanowire model regarding topological superconductivity hosting Majorana $0$- and anomalous $π$-modes, here we theoretically investigate the possible emergence of finite momentum Fulde-Ferrell (FF) superconducting state in quasi-energy of the above model under the periodic modulation of in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields while the static limit does not host a FF ground state. We demonstrate controllable switching between Floquet Majorana $0$- and $π$-modes via reversal of the supercurrent direction, revealing pronounced nonreciprocal supercurrent signatures which is a manifestation of the FF pairing. We validate the onset of FF pairing following a self-consistent mean-field analysis where externally applied supercurrent facilitates nonreciprocal signatures in quasi-energy spectra. The above findings directly indicates to the intriguing phenomenon of superconducting diode effect (SDE). The drive amplitude serves as a parameter to regulate the diode efficiency with chemical potential. Our study thus reveals a rich interplay between Floquet topological superconductivity and finite-momentum FF pairing, providing a tunable way to switch between different Floquet Majorana modes and realize the SDE with high efficiency.
summary: The paper theoretically explores how applying a periodic drive to a Rashba nanowire can induce a finite momentum Fulde-Ferrell superconducting state. This state manifests as pronounced nonreciprocal supercurrents, leading directly to the Superconducting Diode Effect (SDE). The findings demonstrate that this effect is controllable by tuning the driving parameters.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of a finite momentum Fulde-Ferrell (FF) superconducting state in a driven Rashba nanowire, linking this phenomenon to the Superconducting Diode Effect (SDE).
main_result: The periodic drive stabilizes a Floquet-induced FF superconducting state, enabling controllable switching between topological Majorana modes and realizing pronounced nonreciprocal supercurrent signatures indicative of SDE.
method: Theoretical analysis employing the Floquet formalism combined with self-consistent mean-field calculations to determine the superconducting order parameter and current response.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D Rashba nanowire proximitized to an s-wave superconductor, subjected to time-periodic modulation of in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields (Floquet drive).
key_observables:
Nonreciprocal supercurrent signatures ($I^+_c 
eq I^-_c$), Floquet Majorana 0- and $\pi$-modes, diode efficiency ($\eta$), and the finite Cooper pair momentum ($q_0$).
important_parameters: Drive amplitude, chemical potential ($\mu$), and the presence/magnitude of a static magnetic field component ($B_y$) are crucial tuning parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Floquet formalism to treat the time-periodic driving and uses self-consistent mean-field theory for superconducting pairing.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic setups, quasienergy spectra showing topological phase diagrams (0- vs. $\pi$-FMMs), supercurrent density profiles confirming nonreciprocity, and dependence of diode efficiency on driving parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the model Hamiltonian under periodic drive to analyzing the resulting Floquet topology via spectral analysis, followed by self-consistent calculations that confirm finite momentum pairing and quantify the resultant SDE.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from topological superconductivity (Majorana modes) with non-equilibrium transport phenomena (SDE) using time-periodic driving, which is highly relevant for designing novel superconducting electronic devices.

We illustrate the schematic of a 1D Rashba nanowire (green), featuring Rashba SOC of strength α, that is placed in close proximity to a bulk s-wave superconductor (blue) in presence of external Floquet step drive in terms of the mag- netic field B(t) = (Bx(t), By(t)). This setup realizes topo- logical FMMs (red spikes) localized at the end of the NW, accompanied by non reciprocal critical supercurrents I+ c ≠I− c highlighting Floquet induced SDE.

FIG. 2. We depict the spectral properties of the driven Rashba NW model by demonstrating the Floquet quasi-energy spectrum En, computed from Eq. (3), as a function of J′ 1 in panels (a,b) for q = 0.5 and q = −0.5, respectively, with By = 0.6 and J′ 0 = 0.6π. FIG. 3. We demonstrate the Floquet quasienergy spectrum, along with the topological invariant Px, obtained within the self-consistent framework exploting Eq. (7), as a function of the finite Cooper-pair momentum q in panels (a,b,c). Panel (a) depicts the emergence of topological π-FMMs exclusively in the negative-q sector, panel (b) features 0-FMMs in the positive-q sector, while panel (c) simultaneously hosts π-FMMs in the negative-q sector and 0-FMMs in the positive-q sector, highlighting the switching between dynamical topological FMMs in FF phase. The parameter set (J′ 1, J′ 0, µ/J′ 0, By) is chosen as (0.5π, 0.46π, 1.2, 0.45) in panel (a), (0.6π, 0.46π, 1.2, 0.5) in panel (b), and...
